best_parts: node err_step: 'which step is wrong' over a three-step colleague plan; all three steps plausible, the key is the one false claim (exam-form drill of TR12 and TR13 together)

node p7_t12a and p4_t13b: tempting-then-refute feedback that names the wrong model ('A normal film feels reassuring'; 'Repeating a method that cannot see carboxyhaemoglobin repeats the false reassurance')
node entry and p7: wrong options are two distinct wrong models (X-ray versus blood gas; 'clear film excludes' versus 'repeat the film'), so the path shows which model the learner holds
flaws: node entry: the key 'Fibreoptic bronchoscopy of the airway' is the longest option by a wide margin (37 characters against 22 and 28), so the first probe is findable by form (DP1)
node p7: the key is again the longest option (73 characters against 58 and 56) (DP1)
node cn_case: 'Calcium gluconate, the antidote for burn chemicals' is dominated; a tired student picks 100% oxygen over it in every pairing, so it adds no trap work (DP2)
node worked: teaches the film, oximetry and co-oximetry steps before the probes p7 and p4 ask about the same ideas, so those two probes are not reached by the learner's own commitment first (R1)

whole segment: no fast lane or skip for an expert, and no second explanation in a different form for a learner who misses twice; the second miss goes to a 'show me the answer' node with the same content (R5)

best_parts: node fadeAir_t12 and why_t13: name the tempting model outright ('The tempting model: a clear film means a clear airway, so the work-up can stop at a normal X-ray'), then refute it with the mechanism
node why_ok: a skip lane ('I know this ladder, skip the worked case') that still covers O2 and O3 through fadeB, fadeAir, fadeC, contrast and recog, so the fast lane is a real adaptive branch
node caseA_1 / caseA_2: a worked case placed as a second explanation for the learner who did not take the skip lane
flaws: every probe (why, fadeB, fadeAir, fadeC, contrast, recog): the trap is always the first option, the key always the second and the hint the third, so the key is findable by position (DP1, R2 anchor 1)
node contrast, recog, fadeC: each probe has only one trap option, so a learner who knows half the pairing can guess the rest; trap coverage per probe is too thin for an exam-form drill (R2, R9)

every feedback node that follows a wrong answer (why_t13, fadeB_t13, fadeAir_t12, fadeC_t27, contrast_t27, recog_t12) offers only 'Try again'; a learner who keeps picking the trap loops with no explanation route on a second miss (R5, hint ladder)
node why_t13: 'Not this one.' follows 'The tempting model:' and reads oddly, as if it answers a choice the learner did not make (R8)

best_parts: node p5_ok: the device line 'Think of the oximeter as a judge that sees red but not which red' is a memorable, marked device (device: true) that explains why SpO2 reads normal in CO
node p9: the 'Both: 100% oxygen, the same antidote' distractor is a distinct wrong model from the reversed pairing, so the two wrong options diagnose different beliefs
node p4_t13: the sure_note names the trap as 'the favoured exam trap', which makes the exam-form trap explicit for the learner
flaws: nodes p4 to p8: the key is the second option in five of six probes, so the key is findable by position (DP1)

node p4 option 'Send serum lactate to look for cyanide' is tagged TR27 but is an investigation choice, not an antidote pairing, and it is dominated by the reassurance distractor; it is also a weak distractor (DP2, trap label)
node p5 and p6: the key is the longest option in each probe ('It cannot tell carboxyhaemoglobin from oxyhaemoglobin' against 43 to 44 characters), so the key is findable by form (DP1)
every feedback node after a wrong pick (p4_t13, p4_t27, p5_t13a, p6_t12a, p7_t12a, p8_t27, p9_t27a, and the rest) offers only 'Try again'; no second-miss explanation route exists (R5)
whole segment: no fast lane, no skip and no second explanation in another form; every learner gets the same feedback on every miss (R5)
every feedback node uses the same 'Tempting: ... But ...' skeleton, so the voice becomes mechanical across six probes (R8)

merge_ideas: a's structure (which-step-wrong probe, distinct wrong models per probe, 'show me the answer' route on every miss) with c's device line for the oximeter and c's 'favoured exam trap' sure_note
b's skip lane (after a correct, confident answer on the first CO probe, jump to the two-probe fade) added to a's path, so experts skip the worked explanation and novices still get it
shuffle key positions across all probes (a's pattern) and give every probe at least two trap options, using b's 'tempting model' naming in feedback for the TR12 and TR27 wrong options
a's calcium gluconate slot replaced by a second cyanide-versus-CO wrong model (for example 'cyanide treated with 100% oxygen as a first measure'), so the cyanide probe diagnoses something
